description: High-intensity artificial sweetener approximately 200 times sweeter than sucrose.
purposeInFood: Non-nutritive intense sweetener in diet beverages, sugar-free candies, and yogurt.
healthConcerns: IARC classified as 'possibly carcinogenic to humans' (Group 2B). Potential impacts on gut microbiota and insulin sensitivity.
countriesRestrictedOrBanned: Warning labels required in EU & USA for Phenylketonuria (PKU)
sideEffects: Headaches, mood alterations in sensitive individuals, PKU risk
references: WHO IARC Monograph Vol 134 (2023); EFSA Panel on Food Additives (2013)

description: Inorganic white pigment used to brighten or whiten food products.
purposeInFood: Used in confectionery, bakery glazes, sauces, and powdered creamer for brightness.
healthConcerns: Genotoxicity concerns due to nanoparticle accumulation in body tissues. Banned in EU.
countriesRestrictedOrBanned: Banned in EU (EFSA 2021), Restricted in Switzerland
efsaStatus: Banned (No longer considered safe due to genotoxicity)

description: Sodium salt of glutamic acid producing umami savory flavor.
purposeInFood: Flavor booster in savory snacks, instant noodles, processed meats, and soups.
healthConcerns: High sodium content contribution. Symptom complex (headache, flushing, sweating) in sensitive individuals.
countriesRestrictedOrBanned: Restricted limits in infant food across EU/US
sideEffects: Flushing, sweating, facial pressure, blood pressure spikes

whoIarcClassification: Group 1 - Carcinogenic to humans (Ingested Nitrate/Nitrite under conditions leading to nitrosation)
description: Inorganic compound used to cure meats and inhibit Clostridium botulinum.
purposeInFood: Preservative and pink color agent in bacon, sausages, hot dogs, and cured meats.
healthConcerns: Forms carcinogenic N-nitroso compounds (nitrosamines) when cooked at high heat or reacted with proteins.
countriesRestrictedOrBanned: Strict limits in EU, Denmark enforcing lower limits
efsaStatus: Authorized with strict residual limits (ADI 0.07 mg/kg)
fdaStatus: Approved in Cured Meats with limits
sideEffects: Methemoglobinemia risk in infants, nitrosamine formation

scientificName: Enzymatically converted corn starch fructose-glucose syrup
description: Liquid sweetener made from corn starch processed to contain 42% or 55% fructose.
purposeInFood: Sweetener and moisture retainer in soft drinks, pastries, ketchups, and cereals.
healthConcerns: Hepatic de novo lipogenesis, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), insulin resistance, uric acid spike.
countriesRestrictedOrBanned: Subsidies restricted in EU, production quota system
sideEffects: Weight gain, elevated triglycerides, insulin resistance, gout flares

description: Synthetic lemon yellow azo dye derived from petroleum.
purposeInFood: Coloring in soft drinks, candies, jams, chips, and processed cheeses.
healthConcerns: Part of the 'Southampton Six' dyes linked to hyperactivity in children (ADHD) and allergic cross-reactivity with aspirin.
countriesRestrictedOrBanned: Warning required in EU: 'May have an adverse effect on activity and attention in children'
sideEffects: Urticaria, rhinitis, asthma exacerbation, child hyperactivity

description: Synthetic phenolic antioxidant used to prevent rancidity in fats.
purposeInFood: Preserving fats, oils, potato chips, chewing gum, and vegetable oils.
healthConcerns: Endocrine disruptor, suspected human carcinogen (IARC 2B). Toxicity in liver and thyroid.
countriesRestrictedOrBanned: Restricted in Japan, UK infant foods
fdaStatus: Approved as Food Additive with limits
references: NTP 15th Report on Carcinogens; EFSA Journal 2011;9(10):2392

commonName: Mono- and Diglycerides of Fatty Acids
description: Synthetic mixture of glycerol mono- and diesters derived from animal or plant fats.
purposeInFood: Emulsifier in ice cream, bread, margarine, peanut butter, and processed baked goods.
healthConcerns: May contain trace trans fatty acids and glycidyl esters. Potential disruption of intestinal mucus membrane.
countriesRestrictedOrBanned: Allowed globally; source verification required for Halal/Kosher
allergens: May be derived from Soy or Palm oil

description: Finely ground whole oat grains rich in beta-glucan soluble fiber.
purposeInFood: Nutritive grain base for cereals, breads, and healthy snacks.
healthConcerns: None. Promotes heart health and lowers LDL cholesterol.
efsaStatus: Approved Heart Health Claim (Beta-glucan lowers cholesterol)
fdaStatus: Approved Health Claim (Soluble fiber reduces CHD risk)
allergens: May contain cross-contact Gluten if processed on shared equipment

description: Zero-calorie natural intense sweetener extracted from the leaves of Stevia rebaudiana.
purposeInFood: Sweetener in low-sugar drinks, teas, yogurts, and protein bars.
healthConcerns: Safe non-glycemic sweetener. Minimal impact on blood glucose or insulin.
efsaStatus: Authorized (ADI 4 mg/kg bw/day expressed as steviol equivalents)
fdaStatus: High purity steviol glycosides are GRAS
sideEffects: Slight bitter aftertaste in high amounts

purposeInFood: Emulsifier in chocolate, infant formula, bakery goods, and instant powders.
sideEffects: Mild GI distress only in extreme excessive intake

scientificName: Exopolysaccharide produced by Xanthomonas campestris fermentation
description: Natural polysaccharide produced by bacterial fermentation.
purposeInFood: Thickening agent and salad dressing stabilizer, gluten-free baking binder.
healthConcerns: Safe soluble dietary fiber. High amounts may cause mild bloating.
sideEffects: Mild laxative effect in very high quantities (>15g/day)
